newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor lowers '97 sales target.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor lowers '97 sales target.

text.p: The president of South Korea's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday the company's vehicle sales would reach 13 trillion won this year, down from its target of 13.5 trillion won.

"Domestic sales this year are expected to remain at last year's level. Overall economic slowdown is mainly to blame," Hyundai Motor president Park Byung-Jae told Reuters. The company is a flagship unit of the Hyundai Group HYGR.CN.
He said domestic sales would fall to 750,000 units this year, down from its earlier target of 825,000 units.
Hyundai's domestic sales last year were 740,000 units.
Park, however, said the company can meet its export target of 675,000 units this year.
"Our mid-sized sadans and Tiburon sport cars sell well overseas. So I think there will be no problems in meeting export target," he said.
"I believe domestic sales will improve towards the end of this year in line with an economic recovery," he said.
Park said Hyundai's domestic sales would also be helped by its new mini-compact car "ATOZ," to be marketed from September.
ATOZ would take up 70 percent of the mini car segment of the domestic market, he said.

Park also said Hyundai would invest seven percent of its sales in research and development in 1997, against 5.5 percent in 1996. "About 900 billion won will be spent in research activities this year and the investment percentage will be maintained at the level in the future," Park said.
Park said Hyundai's annual production capacity would rise to 2.4 million units by 2000 from the current 1.65 milllion.
"Our production will rise largely in other nations from now on. India, China, Europe and Russia are regions that we think are very important for our expansion projects," Park said.
He said a joint venture plant in Turkey would begin producing sub-compact cars and vans from July at an annual rate of 50,000 units.
"The capacity will soon rise to 100,000 units," he said.
Hyundai also is expected to complete a plant in India with an annual capacity of 200,000 cars by the end of 1998.
Hyundai officials said the $1.1 billion India project would be entirely invested by Hyundai.
Hyundai is scheduled to complete a joint venture plant in Indonesia capable of producing 100,000 units a year by 1999.
"In addition, we are negotiating with China to build a finished car plant," Park said. But he gave no further details.
